---
title: "Method"
description: "How Open Talamh finds, checks and grades land held by Catholic Church entities in Ireland, and the data sources it uses."
toc: true
---

Open Talamh is building the first open, parcel-level atlas of land held by Catholic Church entities in Ireland. Every parcel traces back to a primary record, and every parcel carries a confidence grade. The method is being piloted in County Dublin before it is extended to other counties and, later, to State bodies.

## Principles

- Every claim links to a folio, deed, register entry or published document.
- Every parcel carries a confidence grade, so uncertainty is visible rather than hidden.
- The method, code and list of entities are published, so anyone can re-run or challenge the work.
- The map states facts and sources. Interpretation lives in separate, clearly labelled commentary.
- Releases are versioned with a changelog, and anyone can [submit a correction](contribute.qmd#corrections).

## What counts as "the Church"

The Catholic Church is not one legal owner. Open Talamh defines the entities it tracks and publishes those definitions.

| Class | Typical legal holder | Where names come from |
|---|---|---|
| Dioceses (26) and parishes | Diocesan trusts, named clerical trustees | Charities Regulator, diocesan directories |
| Religious congregations and orders | Trustee bodies, companies limited by guarantee, named trustees | Charities Regulator, CRO, AMRI membership |
| Schools | Patron trustees, boards of management, congregational trusts (e.g. Edmund Rice Schools Trust) | Department of Education school lists, patron bodies |
| Health and care | Voluntary hospital companies, congregational holding companies | HSE Section 38 list, HIQA registers of designated centres, CRO |
| Lay Catholic bodies and diocesan agencies | Companies, trusts | CRO, Charities Regulator |

### The inclusion test

A body is included when it is **part of, or legally controlled by, a Catholic diocese, parish, religious order or lay Catholic association**. Being founded by a priest or a nun, having a Catholic ethos, or meeting in a parish hall is not enough. Every body on the entity list must be backed by a document showing that link, such as a charity registration, a company filing or a diocesan directory.

Included, for example:

- Dioceses, parishes and their trusts, including parish halls and parish centres held by parish trustees.
- Religious orders and congregations, and the companies and trusts that hold their property.
- Lay Catholic associations, such as the Society of St Vincent de Paul, the Pioneer Total Abstinence Association, the Legion of Mary and the Knights of Columbanus.
- Diocesan agencies, such as Crosscare and Accord.
- Nursing homes, hospitals, disability services and colleges, **only where the registered provider or owner is an order, a diocese or a company they control**. Where an order has handed a hospital or college to an independent company or the State, the site is recorded as a former holding.

Not included as entities:

- Scouting Ireland, the GAA, Comhaltas Ceoltóirí Éireann, Lions Clubs and the Simon Community, which have no formal Church link.
- Approved housing bodies, even those founded by religious (such as Respond, Focus Ireland and the Peter McVerry Trust), which are independent. A convent an order sold or gave to one is recorded as a former holding of the order.
- School boards of management, which do not own land. The school's patron or trustees are tracked instead.
- Community halls run by committees.

Land these groups use can still be Church land. A GAA pitch or a Scout den on parish land appears on the map under the parish's folio, because the folio search is on the owner's name, not the user's.

Each parcel is assigned one ownership tier:

- Legal title: A Catholic entity or trustee is the registered owner on a folio.
- Beneficial interest: Title is held by individuals or a company in trust for a Catholic entity.
- Control without title: For example, patronage of a school on State-owned land, or a long lease.
- Former holding: Sold, transferred to the State, or handed over under redress agreements since 2002.

## Confidence grades

| Grade | Evidence | Shown on the map as |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | A Land Registry folio names a Catholic entity as registered owner | Confirmed |
| **B** | A folio names individuals or a company, and a second source confirms they hold in trust for a Catholic entity | Confirmed via trustee |
| **C** | Registry of Deeds evidence only | Probable |
| **D** | Use, signage or a heritage record suggests Church ownership; title not yet checked | Unverified lead (not counted in totals) |
| **E** | Held since 2002 but since sold or transferred | Former holding |

The first Dublin map is built entirely from open data, so every point on it is currently a **grade D lead**.

## How ownership is established

The ground truth is the Land Registry folio: a mapped parcel with a named registered owner. About 93% of the State's land area is registered. A Names Index search returns every folio registered to one exact name in one county, so the unit of work is *name × county*, not parcel.

1. Collect the legal name of every diocese, parish, congregation, trust and school body, with every variant (prefixes such as "Trustees of", Irish-language forms, abbreviations, former names). Keep extending it until a full round of checking new folios produces no new names. The list is published with a version number.
2. Every search is logged, including those that return nothing. Each folio returned is pulled for its owner, burdens and location.
3. Every church, convent, school and institution is looked up on the free Land Registry map to find its folio. Any site whose owner isn't on the name list reveals a missing name. The share of known sites already found in step 2 measures how complete the search is.
4. For land with no folio, the Registry of Deeds is searched by townland and by grantor and grantee name. These results get a lower grade.
5. Every parcel is graded using the A to E scale above.
6. A random sample is double-checked by a second researcher, totals are benchmarked against published figures (such as the 2009 panel valuations and RTÉ's 800-property Christian Brothers portfolio), and each major entity is sent its list of parcels for a right of reply before publication.

### Known blind spots

- Beneficial ownership registers for trusts and companies are not public, so trusts are only visible where a second source links trustee to beneficiary.
- Folios show legal title, not leases, licences or covenants.
- Trustee names change over time, so each folio is recorded with the date it was retrieved.

## Data sources

Location data is plentiful and open, while ownership data is closed and paid. So the work of this project is to bridge the two data sources.

| Source | What it gives | Shows ownership? | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Land Registry folios](https://www.landdirect.ie/) (Tailte Éireann) | Registered owner, burdens, parcel map | **Yes, the ground truth** | Paid per search and per folio; free map search for folio numbers |
| Registry of Deeds, Henrietta Street | Deeds since 1708, by grantor and townland | Clues | In person, by appointment |
| [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/) | Churches, convents, religious land, schools, graveyards | No | Free (ODbL) |
| [National Inventory of Architectural Heritage](https://data.gov.ie/dataset/national-inventory-of-architectural-heritage-niah-national-dataset) | Historic churches, convents, presbyteries and schools, with original and current use | No | Free |
| Council Records of Protected Structures (e.g. [Dublin City](https://data.gov.ie/dataset/dublin-city-record-of-protected-structures), Fingal, South Dublin, Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown) | Protected churches, convents and institutions, described by each council | No | Free |
| Department of Education school lists ([primary](https://data.gov.ie/dataset/primary-schools), [post-primary](https://data.gov.ie/dataset/post-primary-schools)) | Every school with its ethos and location | No (the patron is not always the landowner) | Free |
| [Valuation list](https://tailte.ie/en/valuation/open-data/open-data-information) (Tailte Éireann) | Rateable properties with use, area and location | No; places of worship are often exempt | Free |
| [Charities Regulator register](https://data.gov.ie/dataset/register-of-charities-in-ireland) | Legal names of dioceses, parishes, congregations and trusts | Names only | Free |
| [Companies Registration Office](https://core.cro.ie/) | Companies, directors, former names | Names only | Search free; documents paid |
| Ryan, McAleese and Mother and Baby Homes reports; [Industrial Memories](https://industrialmemories.ucd.ie/) | Institutions, operators, dates | No | Free |
| [PARISH: Preserving And Recording Ireland's Sacred Heritage](https://parishproject.nd.edu/) (Keough-Naughton Institute, University of Notre Dame, with Maynooth University) | A photographic record of the interiors of every Catholic church on the island of Ireland | No | Archive and map not yet published; to be used, with credit, once released |
| [Townland and county boundaries](https://data.gov.ie/en_GB/dataset/townlands-national-statutory-boundaries-ungeneralised-20241) | Statutory boundaries | No | Free (CC BY) |
| [Residential Property Price Register](https://www.propertypriceregister.ie/) | Sale prices since 2010 | No | Free |
| INSPIRE cadastral parcels (Tailte Éireann) | Parcel shapes without owners | No | Licence to be confirmed |

See the [reading list](reading.qmd) for the reports, journalism and research behind this method.

## Publishing and licensing

Data is published under an open licence (CC BY 4.0, with layers derived from OpenStreetMap under ODbL), alongside the code, the entity list and a changelog. Folio boundary maps are subject to Tailte Éireann copyright, so until republication is agreed, parcels are published as points with folio numbers, which anyone can look up. Open Talamh maps organisations, not private individuals, and gives every major entity a right of reply before publication.
